answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using max-flow trust graphs. Systems route interaction capacity along a branching vine of signed peer endorsements, isolating unverified nodes outside an onyx consensus tier. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of maintaining authentic, reciprocal transaction histories across the network cut instead of deploying cheap instances as trivial as a sonnet. However, this graph topology creates severe cold-start penalties for honest new agents.
